summary: Native programs can request one literal standing-seat turn and receive its verified report and actual execution receipts. A normally published fractal/seat-turn ProgramMission is the default graph-lowering worker route.

replay.detail: Native turn identity binds the parent step, attempt and durable key to the full request. Replays adopt only that episode; changed requests refuse. Existing graph work is not adopted or converted.

schema.detail: Native-turn creation metadata and verified program.turn.report claims project through the existing run/step persistence. Successful native child runs can expose the completed current attempt/hash $result separately from resource products.

rules.detail: A live exact parent attempt fences admission, worker mutations and verified completion. Native starts require start native-turn authority; the parent edge is established transactionally before admission and rolls back on refusal. Verified reports are daemon receipts, not additional parent writes. Literal assignee, incarnation, lease, real product checks and standing-seat capacity remain authoritative. Inherited resource membership requires the target's authorized host and context before runnable creation; physical harness reparenting is not claimed.

compatibility.detail: Fractal.lower uses the standard published seat-turn protocol unless an explicit per-agent route overrides it or strictWorkers requires explicit bindings. Original inputs and product requirements travel in collision-safe context; ordered prose constraints remain literal worker instructions. Explicit instruction and agent mappings preserve prototype-named keys as own text inputs. The native host admits agent.turn requests and their cancellation messages. No hidden graph mission or DAG scheduler executes the turn.

downtime.detail: No automatic publication, standing-seat reset or graph-runtime cutover. Existing pinned native bundles retain their existing routes.

manual.detail: Deploy an interpreter that understands native-turn claims, then publish the ordinary fractal/seat-turn mission source before publishing lowerings that use its default route. The fixture is publication source, not an automatic mission registry.

recovery.detail: Durable parent linkage cancels only the owned finite episode and prevents late completion after the parent attempt ends. Explicit freshness retains busy-harness protection. Preserve authoritative native-turn claims and use a supporting interpreter to finish or cancel admitted episodes.
